title: E2 agreement and reference checkpoint form B
instructions: Apply agreement and reference checks to five fresh sentences without assistance.

parts.prompt: Which sentence has correct agreement with a distributive subject?

options.text: Every one of the devices have a serial number.
Every one of the devices has a serial number.
Every one of the devices are carrying a serial number.
Every one of the devices were assigned its number tomorrow.

choice_rationales.A: Devices is inside the of-phrase; every one is singular.
choice_rationales.B: Has agrees with the singular distributive subject every one.
choice_rationales.C: Are follows the nearby plural noun incorrectly.
choice_rationales.D: Were is plural and the tense conflicts with tomorrow.

parts.hint: Protected checkpoint: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: Every one refers to each device separately and therefore takes a singular verb.

parts.prompt: Which sentence correctly identifies the plural head subject?

options.text: The results of the survey shows a clear pattern.
The results of the survey show a clear pattern.
The results of the survey is showing a clear pattern.
The results of the survey has shown a clear pattern yesterday.

choice_rationales.B: Results is plural, so show is correct.
choice_rationales.D: Has is singular and the time phrase is poorly controlled.

parts.hint: Protected checkpoint: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: Survey is inside an of-phrase; the plural head results controls the verb.

parts.prompt: Which sentence correctly agrees with all items in a compound subject?

options.text: A notebook and two pens were left on the front desk.
A notebook and two pens was left on the front desk.
A notebook and two pens has been left on the front desk.
A notebook and two pens is lying on the front desk.

choice_rationales.A: Multiple items joined by and take the plural verb were.

parts.hint: Protected checkpoint: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: The compound subject names more than one item and requires plural agreement.

parts.prompt: Irfan showed the model to Riko, and Riko noticed a missing wheel. Which version is clearest?

options.text: When Irfan showed it to Riko, he noticed that it was missing.
Irfan showed Riko his model, and he noticed his wheel was missing.
When Irfan showed Riko the model, Riko noticed that the model was missing a wheel.
He showed it to him, who noticed it.

choice_rationales.A: He and it each have competing possible referents.
choice_rationales.B: He and his could refer to either person.
choice_rationales.C: The observer and the affected object are both explicit.
choice_rationales.D: The pronouns do not establish the people or object clearly.

parts.hint: Protected checkpoint: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: Naming Riko and the model removes ambiguity without changing the meaning.

parts.prompt: The glass container cracked, not the shelf. Which sentence makes that meaning explicit?

options.text: The container stood on the shelf when it cracked.
While standing on the shelf, the glass container cracked.
It stood on it when it cracked.
The shelf held the container before it cracked there.

choice_rationales.A: It could refer to the container or shelf.
choice_rationales.B: The named subject glass container directly controls cracked.
choice_rationales.C: None of the pronouns has a secure referent.
choice_rationales.D: It can still refer to either noun.

parts.hint: Protected checkpoint: no hint is available.
parts.correct_explanation: Making glass container the subject of cracked fixes the intended reference.
